Sports.title: F1 champion Lando Norris hit with 10-place grid penalty as McLaren know they must go for broke in Belgian GP
Sports.content:
F1 champion Lando Norris hit with 10-place grid penalty as McLaren know they must go for broke in Belgian GP



See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lando Norris’s spluttering world championship defence has been hit by a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Belgian Grand Prix.

But the McLaren driver promised not to let the setback spoil his weekend as he attempts to narrow the 82-point gap to leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris has retired from two races and failed to start one of the nine rounds as his Mercedes engine has been beset by unreliability. It has proved the case again going into Spa, with his car being fitted with a new battery, his fourth – one more than is permitted without incurring a sanction.

McLaren decided to take the hit at this point because the famous track in the Ardennes offers a relatively high possibility of passing opportunities. This is also the last race before a significant upgrade is introduced in Hungary next week.

Norris wants to stay at least on the fringes of the title fight in the hope McLaren manage to make significant strides as the season develops.

‘We will have to wait to see but, comparing us to some of our competitors further back in the field, we will probably have a small straight-line speed advantage,’ said Norris. ‘We should have a good chance.

‘We know it is better to take the penalty here than in Hungary or Zandvoort (home of the Dutch Grand Prix on August 23). I hope it is not the end of my weekend before it starts. I am still confident we can do well.

Lando Norris has retired from two races and failed to start one of the nine rounds this season

‘We have been unlucky losing different bits. I am on the backfoot in terms of spare parts, but that is out of my hands. That’s life. You’ve got to take it on the chin.’

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen, meanwhile, refused to be drawn on his future when pressed during the official press conference.

The Dutchman crashed out at Silverstone fortnight ago with a rear-wing failure and is unsettled by Red Bull’s travails that leave him 103 points off the top.

The 28-year-old has yet to commit to his Austrian team for next season. He could explore a move elsewhere or take a year out to consider his next move. ‘There is nothing to say,’ he insisted.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel has got to find a way to get the best out of his top technical talent ahead of Euro 2028. No other country in the world would leave Phil Foden, Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold at home, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
With Thomas Tuchel’s bid to put a second World Cup star on England’s jersey now in tatters, focus turns to the home Euros of 2028.

Can Tuchel’s England end their long barren run without a trophy on home soil? Daily Mail Sport examines the big questions facing the national game.

ARE WE GOOD ENOUGH?

No, frankly, we are not. Not at the moment anyway. Perhaps the biggest disappointment of England’s time at this World Cup is that the national team still doesn’t have an identifiable style of play good enough to hurt the really good opponents.

After Gareth Southgate’s attempts to build a team in the image of some of our rivals on the continent, Tuchel said he wanted to construct one in the style of a Premier League side but when it came to the big tests, that wasn’t apparent.

Had England held on against Argentina and faced Spain in the final, it could have been embarrassing. We have good players who will get better. Jude Bellingham, Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice, Djed Spence and Anthony Gordon should all improve between now and the next summer tournament. But in terms of our ability to dictate games when it matters and against the best sides, England have stagnated and it’s a worry.

Watching a rerun of the last half hour from Atlanta, Argentina trampled all over us and could have scored four. England had twelve percent possession between scoring their goal and the end of the game. That’s not what a good team does.

Thomas Tuchel has still not given this England team an identifiable style good enough to hurt good teams

Argentina trampled all over England to produce the comeback victory in Atlanta

DECISIONS, DECISIONS...

History and culture don’t win football matches, players and coaches do. To win a tournament takes the right squad and a coach making the right decisions.

England’s World Cup squad was big on vibes and culture but, when it came down to it, low on technical and tactical smarts. This was an England squad that had Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah in it but no Cole Palmer, Phil Foden or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Whoever you blame, there is something fundamentally wrong about that. When England needed it, we didn’t have the player to take control of a football game and dictate its direction and its rhythm.

Whatever happens between now and Euro 2028, we have to find a way to make our best players – our most technically gifted footballers – fundamental to how we play and what we do. Palmer would be in the Spain team so why isn’t he in ours?

CAN HARRY GO AGAIN?

So here we are. Back to the same old subject. Captain Kane had a fabulous tournament for England. Perhaps one of only three players – along with Bellingham and Anderson – to emerge from this World Cup with a mark of more than 6/10. But still England rely on him far too much.

Against Argentina, Kane laboured in the part of the game that really mattered. England needed someone up front to stretch the game. Every time we cleared the ball it came back again. But Tuchel kept Ollie Watkins and Marcus Rashford on the bench until it was too late.

The head coach doesn’t trust his Kane understudies and never has. Watkins played six minutes all tournament while Ivan Toney didn’t get a sniff until he was thrown on at the death against Argentina.

England have two years to find an answer to the problem. Kane will be almost 35 by then so the clock is ticking.

England still rely on Harry Kane far too much and Tuchel has two years to find the answer

WHERE IS THE HOPE?

English football is not short of emerging talent and, as we say, already has players in this World Cup squad with time to improve. Tuchel will hope for some real Arsenal game time for 16-year-old Max Dowman over the next season or so, for example.

Bellingham was only 17 when Gareth Southgate included him in his squad for the Euros of 2020 – delayed a year because of Covid – and he got limited minutes. But it was a vital part of Bellingham’s international education and that should be the path for Dowman now.

Elsewhere, Everton’s Tyler Dibling remains a huge prospect, despite a disappointing first season on Merseyside, while Rio Ngumoha of Liverpool should progress quickly now that Mo Salah is not standing in his way.

There is a worry at centre half. We need a ball carrier in that position. If anyone spots the next John Stones please shout.

ARE WE OVERREACTING?

No, we are not. Other European nations get it right so why can’t we? England came to America to win the World Cup and in terms of their football fell well short.

The statement from the FA that dropped after the whistle on Wednesday lamented the fact that it's ‘heartbreaking to be so close’ but the truth is that the way England played was well short of the required standard.

England fell well short of their ultimate goal of winning their second-ever World Cup

English football continues to face challenges with the schedule and the stakeholders must look again at a winter break. Two of Tuchel’s most important players – title winners Rice and Bukayo Saka – arrived at this tournament broken by the domestic season with Arsenal. Frankly, they played like it.

English football keeps telling itself that it has turned a corner in terms of styles of play, technical aptitude and player welfare. But the problem is that if you keep turning corners you end up back in the same place.

Sports.title: England rugby team forced to MOVE hotels in Buenos Aires - after wild World Cup celebrations kept players awake until the early hours
Sports.content:
England’s rugby team have been forced to switch hotels in Buenos Aires because of the chaos caused by Argentina’s World Cup victory.

Tens of thousands of fans gathered in the Plaza de la República on Wednesday night, celebrating their football team’s 2-1 win over England with a huge street party.

Flares and fireworks were set off throughout the night, with barricades erected outside England’s team hotel to provide additional security.

Steve Borthwick’s side were due to return to the same hotel on Sunday, but Argentina’s progression to the final means the area is braced for more chaos over the weekend.

‘I wouldn't suggest that everybody got a great night's sleep for a lot of hours,’ said Borthwick. ‘There were still fireworks going off at 4am in the morning out there.

‘At the same time, most of us were on the other side of the hotel, so we were prepared for that. There were earplugs given to everybody.

Fans with loud hailers gathered in Buenos Aires to celebrate Argentina's win over England

Fireworks were set off amid joyous scenes in the capital, as thousands of fans hit the streets

‘I went up to the balcony that overlooks everything fairly late and there were still a load of players just watching it and just taking it in. We'd obviously all wanted England to win but having seen a spectacle like that, it's one of the experiences of touring. People jumping up and down for hours in the streets. Fireworks going off. It was something to see.’

Anti-English tensions were high, with flags burned and revellers spotted spraying graffiti about Argentina’s right to the Falkland Islands.

If Argentina beat Spain on Sunday then the celebrations will spill into Monday, meaning England’s team bus would struggle to depart for the airport.

Videos of Henry Pollock goading Argentinean fans from team coach have circulated around the internet, but Borthwick insisted it was all in good spirits.

‘Henry's full of character,’ said Borthwick. ‘We want character in our game and we want character in our squad. This squad really embraces what he brings. We've got some players who wouldn't do that and then you've got Henry who would go and do that. What we do, we embrace it. I think it was in good nature. I think it came from a very good place.’

Pollock has been named on the bench for Saturday’s match in Santiago del Estero, with Borthwick naming an unchanged starting XV.

Sports.title: Feeling like a winner, Leo? Grinning Messi poses with Argentina room-mate in hotel selfie the morning after booking champions' place in World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has been pictured savouring Argentina's dramatic World Cup semi-final victory over England on Wednesday night.

Argentina booked their place in the final after edging past England in a fiery and hard-fought encounter which saw Lionel Scaloni’s side commit 15 fouls and receive three yellow cards.

England had taken the lead through Anthony Gordon, but Messi once again proved the difference, the 39-year-old setting up both of Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez’s goals as the reigning world champions powered past Thomas Tuchel’s side.

Tempers flared after the final whistle, with tensions spilling over between the two sides. England's Jude Bellingham became involved in a heated exchange with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco as players and staff gathered on the pitch.

This morning, Rodrigo De Paul shared a photo on Instagram showing himself and Messi relaxing in bed at the team hotel alongside the caption ‘Buen diaaaaa!!’ (good morning!).

The image showed Messi unwinding with mate tea and a packet of Havanna Leo biscuits, while De Paul sat alongside him. Both wore satisfied expressions as they enjoyed a moment of calm before turning their attention to the final.

Messi was pictured unwinding with mate tea and a packet of Havanna Leo biscuits with Rodrigo De Paul sat alongside him

Messi was later photographed enjoying some downtime with his team-mates in Atlanta

The 29-year-old was instrumental in his side's progression to the World Cup final, providing both assists as Argentina struck late to break the hearts of their English rivals

Messi was later photographed enjoying some downtime with his team-mates in Atlanta.

After the final whistle, Messi reserved praise for the Argentina fans inside the stadium, but added that he believed the last-gasp victory had stemmed from their opponents' dwindling fight.

'We felt a lot of emotion, and when we were drawing, we needed the support of the fans, because we saw that we could win it in 90 minutes,' he said.

'Because we already had the goal, because we entered through the inside, the outside, because we created opportunities with crosses, through line passes, through the inside.

'And we felt they didn't want it anymore and we just kept coming, that's why after the 1-1, the crowd helped us again once more, and as I said, we are happy because it was a close match.

'We always want to win, and also because it takes us to play another World Cup final.'

Meanwhile Thomas Tuchel has come under heavy criticism for his tactics following Gordon's opening goal in the 55th minute, with the manager bringing on a raft of defensive substitutes to see out the game.

Muller, who worked under Tuchel at Bayern Munich for a brief spell between 2023 and 2024, said in a video posted on X: 'Argentina played a hell of a game and I cannot believe and understand how England approached this game, especially after they're leading.

'I cannot understand how they invited Argentina to play one cross after the other in perfect crossing positions.'

Casillas, who lifted the World Cup with Spain in 2010, slammed England's 'cowardly' approach after they managed to hold onto just 12 per cent possession from going ahead to conceding the second goal.

'England score the goal and then sit back – cowardly approach,’ the former Real Madrid star posted on X.

'They haven’t left their own box and have allowed Argentina to come forward more. The logical outcome happens.

‘England lost the match all by themselves with that approach. They let Argentina do whatever they wanted. That can’t happen. The final will be incredible.’

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's 'patient' transfer window strategy: Why Andrea Berta is unfazed by lack of business, how 'machine' is working round the clock to secure bargains and the defender who could replace sidelined William Saliba
Sports.content:
‘Patience’ is the buzzword circulating around Arsenal’s London Colney base.

That might not appease large sections of the Premier League champions’ fanbase, with many supporters panicking at their lack of business so far.

But Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta are taking a measured approach, shaped by the unique challenges of a World Cup year and the need to carefully manage a squad already pushed to its physical limits.

The fan expectation stems from a more restrained strategy than last summer, when Berta had made six of his eight signings in July.

Those additions were Kepa Arrizabalaga, Martin Zubimendi, Christian Norgaard, Noni Madueke, Cristhian Mosquera and Viktor Gyokeres. They not only brought with them a great deal of excitement, but those moves left other clubs to sweat on deals, with Arsenal having done the bulk of their business way ahead of the deadline.

At present, the Gunners have only made one outfield signing heading towards the fourth week of July – and that was making Piero Hincapie’s loan deal permanent.

Arsenal made a raft of signings last July, including Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres (pictured), but have made a slower start to this summer's window

Sporting director Andrea Berta with new back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier - the only fresh face in their 2026-27 squad as it stands

Goalkeeper Illan Meslier was signed on a free transfer from Leeds last week. He is expected to be third-choice between the sticks, behind David Raya and Kepa, but could be bumped up to second if the latter departs.

The World Cup has made negotiating deals tricky, with players focused on representing their country. With the tournament concluding on Sunday, there is an expectation that business at Arsenal will start to be ramped up from next week.

Berta has put in the groundwork. Sources say he’s a ‘machine’ who gets to the training ground early in the morning and doesn’t leave until late.

The Italian’s strategy will not be shaken by the lack of signatures so far. He negotiates multiple deals for a single position before pulling the trigger and deciding which player to move for.

It goes back to his days as a banker, a real-world business outlook transported into football. Each agent or club is left on edge wondering if Arsenal really want their player, reducing the likelihood of them strongarming the Gunners into paying way over the odds.

The approach is smart but not flawless. The dithering can cause a player to have his head turned elsewhere, to a different club who show more concrete interest — and more money. Jeremy Monga is a pertinent example, the 17-year-old set to join Arsenal before Manchester City swooped in with a better financial package.

Arsenal, though, have a different sway compared to many clubs. They are the reigning champions, which is a highly attractive proposition for suitors.

It’s understood that Berta refuses to be drawn into a deal which is not good monetary value for the club. The numbers matter to him, a different approach to some sporting directors who are more gung-ho financially.

Berta puts in the groundwork. Sources say he’s a ‘machine’ who gets to the training ground early in the morning and doesn’t leave until late

Left wing is a key area in which Arsenal need to strengthen now Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas

Left wing is the key focus now Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas, with the club closing in on Club Bruges winger Christos Tzolis. Berta’s assistant Maurizio Micheli watched the 24-year-old play for Greece against Sweden last month.

Even when the Gunners get their deal for Tzolis over the line, there is still capacity to bring in another forward, with firm interest remaining in Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers.

The squad needs bolstering. There is an awareness at the club that the opening weeks of the league season present a need for immediate rotation, with many of their frontline players at breaking point.

Declan Rice was the Arsenal outfield player who accumulated the most minutes during the 2025-26 campaign, with 3,094 in the Premier League alone. He has battled through England’s World Cup with neural pain in his hamstring, which began around Christmas.

Bukayo Saka started 25 of Arsenal’s 38 league matches last season despite enduring injuries to his hamstring, hip and achilles. The achilles issue has plagued the winger since March, Thomas Tuchel revealing that Saka had carried on playing for Arsenal while not fully fit in the later months of the league campaign.

He added that the winger would be treated with care in his camp, a genuine concern given that the 24-year-old has played an awful lot of football in the past year. Saka made just two starts in England’s seven World Cup matches, and was an unused substitute in the 2-1 semi-final defeat by Argentina.

William Saliba has been dealing with a back issue which saw the 25-year-old manage just 30 minutes of France’s 2-0 semi-final loss to Spain on Tuesday. He trudged off the pitch, mouthing: ‘My back is gone’.

William Saliba will be out for months after trudging off in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain with a back issue

Arsenal will need to manage their squad carefully this season, with both Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice looking exhausted in the US

It’s understood that Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa is on Arsenal’s radar. He would have the potential to compete with Mosquera as the starting centre back in place of Saliba, who is set to miss at least the first few months of the season. However, the two clubs are some way apart in their valuations of the centre back.

Arsenal’s pre-season officially starts on Monday at London Colney, though players not at the World Cup are currently in a Marbella camp with Arteta and his staff.

For Arsenal, the message remains clear: patience will win out over panic. The next few weeks will determine whether Berta’s calculated approach delivers the final pieces Arteta needs to defend their title.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner's to-do list: The gap in Nottingham Forest squad he's close to filling, keeping Evangelos Marinakis happy - and the line at his unveiling that set him apart from his predecessors
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner's to-do list: The gap in Nottingham Forest squad he's close to filling, keeping Evangelos Marinakis happy - and the line at his unveiling that set him apart from his predecessors

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Forest camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Oliver Glasner has been at Nottingham Forest for only three days but already his in-tray is filling up.

The Austrian has five weeks to reconfigure his team’s tactics, establish who he can rely on and – crucially – identify his principal centre forward for the campaign ahead.

Glasner cut a relaxed figure when he was introduced to the media at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the main challenges facing Glasner as he tries to ensure his team hit the ground running when they face Leeds on August 22.

Oliver Glasner cut a relaxed figure at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief

The Austrian has had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system and it would be a surprise if he deviated from it significantly at Nottingham Forest

The missing pieces

At Crystal Palace, Glasner had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system that proved hugely effective on the counter-attack – though breaking down defensive teams was often a problem.

He insists he has yet to decide between a back three and a back four and was at pains to say he does not want to create ‘Palace Two’ at Forest. Yet given the success he had in south London, it would be a surprise to see Forest line up radically differently.

Glasner intends to play with two No 10s behind a lone front man. Expect one of these to be Morgan Gibbs-White – assuming the Forest captain stays – with the other spot up for grabs. Forest are pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall strongly.

Glasner namechecked Omari Hutchinson and James McAtee in his opening remarks, referencing Hutchinson’s ability to cut inside and shoot on his left foot. As long as Hutchinson has a decent pre-season, we can expect him to figure strongly in the early weeks of the new campaign.

Yet where Hutchinson improved as the season progressed, McAtee struggled throughout and made only 13 starts – two in the league. Just because McAtee is praised by the manager on July 16, that does not guarantee he will be at Forest when the summer window closes.

Perhaps, though, Glasner could be the coach to bring the best from McAtee, who is talented but suffers in the ultra-athletic modern game. If he has mentioned McAtee, it is because Glasner believes he can improve him.

Morgan Gibbs-White will almost certainly be one of Glasner's No10s behind the striker

Elliot Anderson was sold to Manchester City for £116million and Glasner accepts he cannot replace him with one player only. Xaver Schlager is set to join on a free transfer after leaving RB Leipzig and may line up alongside Ibrahim Sangare in the middle of the park, with the Ivory Coast star set to sign a new deal.

While there are plenty of defensive options, right back and No9 are key.

There is an acceptance at Forest that due to his injury record, Ola Aina needs a proven alternative, while Chris Wood turns 35 in December. Forest will be prepared to invest significantly in both areas, and Glasner sidestepped questions about whether he would target Palace players. Daniel Munoz and Jean-Philippe Mateta would certainly help this squad, though.

Glasner’s bold approach

Since Steve Cooper transformed Forest in 2021, leading them from the bottom of the Championship to promotion later that season, all managers have followed him in leaning heavily into Forest’s history.

The club won consecutive European Cups in 1979 and 1980 under Brian Clough, and memories of those days are on display across the City Ground. It would have been easy for Glasner to celebrate that as his predecessors did. He chose not to.

‘It’s a club with huge history but if we all lived as we did 46 years ago, we would fail,’ he said. ‘It’s good to have a great history but great history doesn’t tell anything about the future.

‘We want to make a step forward. Now is our fifth year in the Premier League and it doesn’t make sense talking about the European Cup trophies. Let’s get consistency into Forest in every way.’

It was a bold step and proves Glasner is not here to toe the line. Having won four major trophies (three with Palace and one with Frankfurt) Glasner has huge confidence in his own ability and is not afraid to show it.

Nor will he be afraid to put pressure on the ownership, or to make his feelings known if he is not given what he believes he needs. Indeed, there were plenty of clashes like these during his two-and-a-half years at Palace.

Unlike his predecessors, Glasner did not pay lip service to Forest's European Cup wins under Brian Clough

‘It’s important we stick to what we tell each other as it builds trust and we all want to feel that,’ said Glasner. ‘It’s like friendships or relationships. If someone tells you something and doesn't stick to their word, you don’t trust them anymore.’

Evangelos Marinakis does not mind the odd forthright back-and-forth with a manager and with Glasner, he will surely have his fair share.

Aiming high

Marinakis is the most ambitious owner in the Premier League, bar none. He believes Forest can break into the wealthy elite and become Champions League regulars. As Glasner acknowledged: ‘He is one of the few people I’ve met who are more ambitious than I am and that’s quite difficult. We will challenge each other with our ambition.’

It is very easy in July to talk about stability and consistency. It is a little more difficult if a club invests heavily and are 14th in the table at Christmas. Glasner pointed out that Forest’s league finishes had not always reflected their transfer spending and it is now for him to put that right.

In theory, Glasner’s brief will be to turn Forest into a club who compete regularly in the top half of the table and eventually push for Europe. In practice, he will be expected to hit the ground running.

Talented centre back Murillo will stay at the City Ground unless Forest receive an offer wildly above his market value

Unless they receive offers wildly above their market values, Forest have no plans to sell Gibbs-White, Neco Williams or Murillo. In return, Marinakis will expect no struggles in the bottom half of the table.

Glasner will not worry about these tasks. He has already chosen a difficult route by opting for Forest, who are disliked intensely by Palace these days after the Eagles were demoted to the Conference League a year ago due to UEFA rules, allowing Forest to step into the Europa League. He does not worry, he insists, about whether he’ll become Forest’s fifth managerial casualty in a relatively short time, after Nuno Espirito Santo, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira.

One word of advice, though, Oliver: get a couple of wins on the board early.

Sports.title: FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out
Sports.content:
FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out

The Falkland Islands Government wrote to FIFA expressing their 'disappointment' after Argentina's players unfurled an 'insensitive' banner after beating England in the World Cup semi-finals

View 2 Images Argentina's players held a banner which translated to 'The Falklands are Argentine' (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

FIFA are investigating after Argentina's players displayed what the Falkland Islands Government described as an 'insensitive' banner following their win against England. A late comeback in Atlanta saw Argentina snatch a 2-1 victory, sending them through to the World Cup final.

‌



During the full-time celebrations, a group of Argentina players held up a banner which read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine)." It comes after Argentina's players sung a chant referencing the Falklands in the wake of their 3-2 victory over Egypt in the round of 16.

‌



The banner has sparked backlash from the UK, with many believing that it was offensive to the 255 British soldiers who were killed during the Falklands War in 1982. A statement from the UK Government issued on Thursday morning reiterated: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

‌



Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats, even called for any players who celebrated with the banner to be 'barred from' Sunday's final against Spain. The Falkland Islands Government has also written to football's global governing body.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

England miss out on £18m payday immediately after Argentina heartbreak READ MORE :

England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season READ MORE :

FIFA responded to the backlash by saying: "As is standard procedure, FIFA's independent Disciplinary Committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps."

‌



The aforementioned letter read: "The Falkland Islands Government is disappointed - though regrettably not surprised - that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final - a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

"That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982 which left many traumatised. The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.

View 2 Images The banner has sparked backlash from the UK and Falkland Islands (Image: Jewel SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport. Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.

"We welcome the UK Government's supportive statement this morning. As Business Secretary Peter Kyle highlighted, the World Cup has as one of its central tenets that politics is separate from football. We hope FIFA will make good on their promise to keep politics out of sport, and sanction all behaviour of this nature in line with its own rules."

Sports.title: Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Newmarket Nap
Sports.content:
Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Newmarket Nap

Newsboy fancies his Nap, Roase Of Honour, to win at Newmarket and also hopes Chapter can score at Wolverhampton and complete his Daily Double

View 2 Images Newmarket hosts a seven-race meeting on Friday evening when Newsboy’s nap, Rose Of Honour, is fancied to win the 8.08 (Image: Getty Images)

ROSE OF HONOUR (8.08, Nap) is fancied to bounce back to form and land the Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap at Newmarket on Friday evening.

‌



The James Tate-trained daughter of Night Of Thunder won both her starts as a two-year-old last September, landing six-furlong novice stakes at Kempton Park and Southwell. My selection then made it three from three when beating Papa Cocktail by a neck in a handicap over the same trip at Doncaster at the start of May. Rose Of Honour lost her unbeaten record when 10th of 15 behind Argentine Tango in the Listed Land O’Burns Fillies’ Stakes at Ayr last time out – but there are reasons to expect better here. Not only was she stepping up in class, but the step back to five furlongs and a first encounter with soft ground presented new challenges. Back in handicaps, on quicker terrain and returning to six furlongs, Hector Crouch’s mount can show her true colours.

‌

Sports.title: Man Utd's new wonderkid breaks silence on transfer as fans beg for announcement
Sports.content:
Man Utd's new wonderkid breaks silence on transfer as fans beg for announcement

Manchester United have already made several moves to strengthen their squad this summer under Michael Carrick but supporters are demanding a deal is announced for one player in particular

View 2 Images Michael Carrick could have Cristian Orozco to call upon one day (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

New Manchester United signing Cristian Orozco has opened up on his move to Old Trafford - with fans begging for the club to announce his arrival. The midfielder's move to United was sealed on Monday when he celebrated his 18th birthday.

‌



The Red Devils reached an agreement with Fortaleza CEIF to sign Orozco nine months ago. However, the deal outlined that he would join in the summer transfer window, as he needed to be 18 to complete the move.

‌



United have signed the Colombian teenager because they believe he possesses first-team potential. The team's midfield issues, partly solved by the signings of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, could open the door for him to play under Michael Carrick next season.

‌



Man Utd to press ahead with £30m transfer if Marcus Rashford deal goes through READ MORE :

Man United 'discuss' Real Madrid transfer as Michael Carrick eyes another midfielder READ MORE :

Orozco has started life at United by joining the academy, and he will be assessed by coaches before his next steps are decided. The young star playing for the Under-21s this season is the most likely outcome.

United will be patient with Orozco as he settles into his new surroundings. The club has made similar signings over the last 18 months, having signed Sekou Kone from Mali and Diego Leon from Paraguay.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



And Orozco has now spoken to ESPN Colombia about his transfer, explaining what fans can expect. He said: “I know my strengths are my physicality and my technique.

"I have those qualities and, with the gift God gave me, I don’t think it will be too difficult. But everything is about adapting. I’m very young and that’s what I’ll need to do."

View 2 Images Cristian Orozco is United's latest midfield signing (Image: Noushad Thekkayil/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



United will provide English lessons for Orozco to help him settle in. Referencing his visit to Carrington in December, he said: “I expect to learn a lot of English. When I was there, I realised just how, how important it is.

“I want to arrive and learn as quickly as possible. That’s what’s required so I can show my level and everything I’m capable of. I want to adapt to everything that comes my way as quickly as possible."

Orozco's signing has got fans excited on social media platform X with supporters begging the club to announce that he has joined them. One said before the club announced Karl Darlow's and Santos' signing, "Can you please just announce Santos, Darlow and Orozco."

‌

Orozco was welcomed to Manchester in the winter and shown around Carrington and Old Trafford. The trip included a taste of training sessions with United's academy teams.

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm Jeremy Jacquet shirt number as new transfer seizes on major exit
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm Jeremy Jacquet shirt number as new transfer seizes on major exit

Jeremy Jacquet has started training with his new team-mates at Liverpool, who paid £60million to sign him from Rennes in the January transfer window before completing his move this summer

View Image Jeremy Jacquet has been given his shirt number (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool have announced that new signing Jeremy Jacquet will wear the No.5 shirt. French defender Jacquet inherits the number from Ibrahima Konate, who left Anfield upon the expiry of his contract in June.

‌



The France international went on to join Real Madrid on a free transfer, but Liverpool already had his replaced lined up. The Reds shelled out £60million to sign Jacquet from Rennes in January.

‌



But the 21-year-old remained with the Ligue 1 club until the end of the season. Now, Jacquet is training with his new team-mates and showed off his new shirt in a video posted on Liverpool's social media channels.

‌



Konate was given the No.5 shirt after arriving from RB Leipzig in 2021, taking it from Georginio Wijnaldum. Former Liverpool stars Alan Hansen, Mark Lawrenson and Steve McManaman have also sported the number.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jacquet hopes to become a legend like fellow defender Hansen, with big things expected of him. In an interview with club media, the ex- Clermont Foot loanee beamed: " It's a legendary club, and the football philosophy and project really appealed to me. My family and I believe we have made the right choice and we feel really happy here."

‌



Having missed the end of last season for Rennes with a shoulder injury, Jacquet is now fully recovered. "I feel much improved and I will be 100 per cent ready [for the start of pre-season] because I'm a little ahead of schedule," he explained.

"I was given the go-ahead to start a programme of training with the group [at Rennes], but it was a bit late to be with the team. But with continued hard work I'll be fully fit before the season."

Who else should Liverpool sign? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

He's set to partner Virgil van Dijk at the heart of Liverpool's defence, a role which he's relishing. "Of course, I'm really excited to line up alongside a great player like him," Jacquet added. "I think he's up there with the best centre-backs in the world currently, so I can only learn from him."

The Reds' other summer signing, Victor Munoz, is still away at the World Cup with Spain, who'll face Argentina in the final on Sunday. New manager Andoni Iraola confirmed on Monday that Liverpool remain in the market for more signings.

Article continues below

Speaking at his first press conference, Iraola said: "We've signed two players already but we need more players. The club are working on this."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi bathes baby Lamine Yamal in weird throwback snaps ahead of World Cup final showdown
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi bathes baby Lamine Yamal in weird throwback snaps ahead of World Cup final showdown

In 2007, the parents of Spain's Lamine Yamal won a competition to meet a Barcelona player when their son was a baby - and the player in question was Messi, then 20 and a rising star of the team

View 5 Images Messi with baby Lamine Yamal (Image: AP)

Lionel Messi faces Spain's teen prodigy in the World Cup final - 19 years after their first extraordinary encounter.

‌



In 2007, the parents of Spain's Lamine Yamal won a competition to meet a Barcelona player when their son was only five months old. And the player in question was Messi, then 20 and a rising star of the team and Argentina, who defeated England in the 2026 World Cup semi-final.

‌



Joan Monfort documented the meeting in a series of photographs. They resurfaced two years ago, when Yamal helped Spain win Euro 2024, as his father posted one online with the caption "The beginning of two legends".

‌



In the photos, a smiling Messi is cradling and bathing a tiny baby boy who would inexplicably follow so closely in his footballing footsteps.

"It is a true miracle of destiny," Monfort said. "It is serendipity - when you find something extra special, so much bigger than you ever thought. If you wrote this in a film it would not seem possible."

View 5 Images The parents of Spain's Lamine Yamal won a competition to meet Messi when their son was only five months old.

‌



Lionel Messi takes advantage of FIFA rule vs England with double World Cup prize in sight READ MORE :

Mark Chapman flies home from World Cup as BBC host misses final round of matches READ MORE :

The photoshoot took place in the away dressing room at Barcelona's Camp Nou stadium. Yamal's family had won a competition to be there.

His parents, Moroccan-born Mounir Nasraoui and Sheila Ebana from Equatorial Guinea, met after moving to Barcelona as children with their own families. Yamal is their eldest child, and shortly after he was born, they entered a raffle run by Catalan newspaper Sport in conjunction with Barcelona shirt sponsor and international children's charity Unicef.

Those selected at random would have professional photos taken of their baby with a Barcelona first-team player. Yamal was among the winners, and on the day the family arrived, they were paired with Messi by chance.

‌



View 5 Images Messi helping to bathe Lamine Yamal, who was merely six months old at the time with Yamal's mother Sheila Ebana (Image: AP)

"I had no idea it was Yamal in the photo until one my friends called me in 2024 and told me his father had posted it to Instagram," Monfort recalled. "Messi is a really introverted guy, very timid and shy.

"He came into the dressing room and suddenly had to take these photos with a little baby - not even a kid, a proper baby and his face changed like he had no idea what to do! It is difficult for a young man, but Lamine was a very happy, smiley little baby.

‌



"His mum Sheila helped us, she was a young girl and they were a very poor family, but they were very nice to work with.

"Messi was always a professional in these kinds of things and he adapted to the situation very quickly." Messi still wore number 19 for Barcelona in 2007, only inheriting the number 10 shirt a year later when Ronaldinho left the club."

View 5 Images Messi faces Spain's Lamine Yamal in the final - 19 years after their first extraordinary encounter. Yamal's parents won a competition to meet a Barcelona player in 2007 when Yamal was five months old. (Image: AP)

‌



By his 19th birthday Messi had scored 11 career goals and won La Liga and the Uefa Champions League once each. Having turned 19 on Monday, Yamal has already scored a whopping 56 goals and won La Liga three times and the Copa del Rey once, as well as Euro 2024.

Yamal is not actually the player's surname, but the second of his two first names. His full name is Lamine Yamal Naraoui Ebana, and he wears the former two on the back of his shirts for both Barcelona and Spain as an homage to two people who helped his family around the time of his birth.

View 5 Images Yamine Lamal in the semi-final win against France (Image: AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

‌



It has been widely reported in Spanish media that Yamal's father promised to name him after two friends who assisted the family financially, helping them to pay their bills at a time when money was tight.

Lamine is a common male first name in Arabic. It can be translated to English as honest or trustworthy. Yamal is a variant of Jamal, meaning elegance or beauty.

He grew up in Rocafonda, a working-class neighbourhood in Mataro, 20 miles north of Barcelona. Yamal has celebrated some of his goals by making a 3-0-4 gesture with his fingers, referring to Rocafonda's postcode.

Article continues below

Yamal told El Pais in earlier in the tournament: "What my mother has done, what my father has done, I couldn't have done that for anyone who is not my child. If you don't have money, it's very hard to help your child play football.

"And my parents managed to make all that happen. It's something I'll never be able to repay them for."

Sports.title: The 31 dirty tricks Argentina used against England - full comprehensive list
Sports.content:
England's World Cup quest came to an agonising close after Argentina came from behind to knock them out in the penultimate stage. However, Lionel Scaloni's side will contest Sunday's final against Spain having used every tool at their disposal.

When all is said and done, the onus lies with Thomas Tuchel and his men for not doing enough to get the job done in Atlanta. After all, they would have been within their rights to fight fire with fire and deploy the same dark arts as their opponents.

That doesn't make it any easier to swallow a particularly bitter pill, however. And it becomes that much more difficult to accept when breaking down the sheer quantity of underhanded offences Argentina were guilty of en route to a 2-1 comeback win.

What did you make of Argentina's dirty tactics? Did they cross the line, or is all fair in love and war? Have your say below!

‌



1 min

Alexis Mac Allister catches Elliot Anderson after pressing him just 19 seconds into the semi-final.

2 mins

Tensions rise when Leandro Parades unnecessarily shoves Jude Bellingham in the back, prompting the Real Madrid man to respond verbally, with players from both sides getting involved.

Thomas Tuchel told FIVE 'facts' about England vs Argentina as his decisions are ripped apart READ MORE :

Lionel Messi takes advantage of FIFA rule vs England with double World Cup prize in sight READ MORE :

3 mins

Argentina's strategy to disrupt England's build-up play becomes evident when Enzo Fernandez arrives late on Anderson just moments after the match restarts.

6 mins

Anderson is involved again when Giuliano Simeone, the son of Beckham's nemesis Diego, catches the back of Anderson's foot.

‌



11 mins

England players start to retaliate when Fernandez escapes punishment for another foul on Anderson before a brief grappling match on the floor.

View 5 Images Thomas Tuchel couldn't believe some of the officiating he saw in Atalanta (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

11 mins

At the same time, a recovering Morgan Rogers is tripped.

13 mins

Following an offside flag against Simeone, Jordan Pickford collides with him while attempting to retrieve the ball, prompting the midfielder to flick his boot towards the England keeper.

‌



15 mins

Leandro Paredes executes a robust challenge on Bellingham, who is then on the receiving end of a verbal volley.

16 mins

Anthony Gordon surges forward only to be hauled down by Simeone, who delivers a condescending pat on the head.

24 mins

Referee Ismail Elfath warns Simeone at a corner against obstructing Pickford, only for him to do precisely that. Elfath blows his whistle for an infringement as the set-piece is delivered.

‌



28 mins

Mac Allister arrives late on Reece James, but no foul is awarded, prompting Tuchel to lose his cool on the touchline.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

31 mins

Fernandez becomes the third player in quick succession to foul Bellingham after the England midfielder had evaded Simeone.

View 5 Images There was pre-match speculation concerning Ismail Elfath and his history refereeing Lionel Messi (Image: Getty Images)

‌



33 mins

Marc Guehi positions himself ahead of Simeone and, during the tussle for possession, the winger leads with his head while attempting to impede him.

34 mins

Argentina right-back Nahuel Molina joins the fray by barging into Bellingham's back.

36 mins

Messi weaves his way past Kane and Gordon before Anderson crashes into him, earning the match's first yellow card. Messi aims a slight kick towards Djed Spence, which goes unnoticed.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



37 mins

Kane covers his mouth to speak to the referee as Anderson is receiving his yellow card, leading to Mac Allister and Paredes frantically pleading for him to be sent off. However, a player cannot be red-carded for covering their mouth while talking to the referee, only for speaking confrontationally to an opponent.

41 mins

As Rogers tries to counter-attack, Lisandro Martínez hauls him back, with the referee finally booking a player in blue.

45+1 mins

As James attempts to take a quick throw with a new ball, someone from the Argentina bench hurls the old one back onto the pitch in an attempt to waste time.

45+2 mins

Paredes leaves a high boot on Anderson just as the first half draws to a close.

‌



View 5 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino was in attendance to see the list of contentious calls in person (Image: Getty Images)

Half-time

Messi and Fernandez surround the referee to complain about something. Messi continues his protests as the pair head down the tunnel.

48 mins

Bellingham closes down Messi at the byline and, as the pair tumble off the pitch, Messi shoves the England midfielder and into the advertising board.

51 mins

The Argentina player most likely to pick up a yellow card finally gets one as Cristian Romero is cautioned for dragging Bellingham to the ground rugby-style to thwart a counter-attack.

‌



53 mins

Simeone swings an arm behind him and it catches Spence flush in the face but no card is shown.

Has Thomas Tuchel actually improved England? Data reveals familiar Gareth Southgate pattern READ MORE :

58 mins

As Pickford attempts to collect the ball, Romero remains upright rather than ducking. The Everton goalkeeper goes over him and hits the deck hard.

View 5 Images It appeared somewhat obvious Jude Bellingham was being targeted by the Argentina players (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

73 mins

After the hydration break, Messi has a nibble at Spence as the Tottenham man tries to take a throw.

‌



85 mins

Following Fernandez's equaliser, Romero celebrates by screaming directly in Pickford's face.

88 mins

John Stones is forced to the ground with a head injury, halting play as the Argentina players surround the referee to complain - again.

90+2 mins

Bellingham attempts to drive England forward, but as the ball goes out for a throw-in. Gabriel Montiel gets in his face to hurl a torrent of abuse at him.

90+7 mins

With England now trailing, Emiliano Martinez clutches a high ball before going to ground to run down the clock, wearing a broad grin throughout.

‌

Argentina's boisterous celebrations infuriate several England players. Dean Henderson shoves Lautaro Martinez, while Rogers becomes embroiled with a cluster of players, and Bellingham slaps substitute Valentin Barco around the back of the head.

Celebrations

Argentina players parade a banner, thrown by supporters, bearing the message: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas," which could land the country's football association in hot water.

Sports.title: England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season
Sports.content:
Here are England’s player ratings from the World Cup.

Let’s not forget this squad reached only England’s third semi final since winning the World Cup in 1966, and produced one of the most epic away displays in the Three Lions history, with their Estadio Azteca triumph against co-hosts Mexico.

There were some standout performers across the seven games that mattered. But some players could also have done a lot better.

And that, sadly, is a reflection of England’s tournament.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

ENGLAND PLAYER RATINGS

Jordan Pickford

The high point was Mexico but this was not vintage Pickford. He made the defence nervous with the ball at his feet. He did not look assured. Could he have done better on Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser against Argentina? I thought that was unstoppable but in previous tournaments, we didn't even question him.

Interesting times ahead with James Trafford eyeing No.1.

‌



Rating: 6

Reece James

His tournament highlights that it is hard to rely on him because of his fitness record and it is hard to argue he was at his best when he played. He missed too much of the tournament to say his inclusion was a success.

England need a more reliable right back.

‌



Rating: 6

View 7 Images Reece James injury issues reared their head again

Ezri Konsa

Blimey, what a kick in the teeth that he did not start the semifinal having played so well in the previous games.

‌



Thomas Tuchel loves him for his tenacity, reading of danger and he showed all of those things. Good, often underrated defender.

Rating: 7.5

John Stones

The two-on-one break against Norway was peak John Stones. People who criticise Alexander Sorloth miss the point. Stones gave him nowhere to go. It was incredible defending.

‌



Having missed much of the season, he was rusty and yet, unlike James, his inclusion was fully justified. Someone is going to get a hell of a free transfer. An England great.

His dressing room prank was a belter, too.

Rating: 7.5

Marc Guehi

‌



It was a shock when he was left out of the opening game against Croatia. And, frankly, sometimes by not playing, your value to the team becomes clearer. It did with Guehi.

So calm, classy and composed. You can see why Man City went all out for him. He has a long England career ahead. Class act.

Rating: 7.5

View 7 Images Marc Guehi celebrates England's win against Mexico (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Nico O’Reilly

Mixed bag. Not sure he ever hit the heights he reached with Man City last season but was solid and decent.

He was unlucky to get dropped a couple of times but that was a reflection of a lack of cohesion on the left plus a reminder that he is not actually a natural full back.

Rating: 6

‌



Dan Burn

Dan Burn summed it up. If I don’t come on, he said, then England are on the way to the World Cup final. Sadly, he came on. Heroics in Mexico (when we never thought he’d get a minute) and as a last-gasp substitute. But more cult figure than class.

We love Burn because it gives everyone hope. That’s lovely - but patronising all at the same time.

Has Thomas Tuchel actually improved England? Data reveals familiar Gareth Southgate pattern READ MORE :

Rating: 6

‌



Jarell Quansah

Defined by his red card in Mexico. Moments like that can cost your team and if you lose then you are the villain. He is a good player, classy defender, a good centre-half.

But not a right back.

Rating: 5

‌



View 7 Images Jarell Quansah was sent off for this challenge on Mexico's Jesus Gallardo

Djed Spence

Played the game of his life against Argentina. And made brilliant substitute appearances against Croatia and Norway.

What a boost this can give his confidence, career and his future. His tackle late on against Argentina - which he celebrated as if he had scored - was iconic. Sad that he got cramp just when Lionel Messi popped up. Spence v Messi. No-one would have dreamed that before the World Cup.

‌



Rating: 8

Elliot Anderson

Good tournament. Completed a £116m move to Manchester City midway through and suddenly he put a few of the doubts about his price to bed. You are worth what someone is willing to pay. He is top class.

Good passing, incredible energy and unstoppable engine. He has enhanced his reputation big time.

‌



Rating: 8

View 7 Images Elliot Anderson reacts to England's World Cup exit - but he had a fine tournament (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice

His game against Mexico was hugely impressive. But, let’s be clear, the guy was running on empty - especially after getting food poisoning in Mexico.

‌



He needs a bloody good holiday. Not his best tournament but never lets England down.

Rating: 7

Jordan Henderson

Made history by becoming the first England player to play at a men’s World Cup. Finished it by breaking his arm after falling over advertising hoardings.

‌



One that he will want to forget. Good for morale.

Rating: 5

Jude Bellingham

Where to start? England’s best player by a mile. He is a national treasure, reminded us what it means to play for England and dominated games.

‌



What a tournament he had. Outstanding. All that pre-tournament nonsense about him not being a team player. He gave everything for the team.

His levels were off the charts. His performance in Mexico was the best I’ve seen in the flesh from an England player. His run of games the best since the lads of 66.

Rating: 9.5

View 7 Images Jude Bellingham scored six goals for the Three Lions (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

‌



Morgan Rogers

A bit-part player really but actually enhanced his standing. His assist for Anthony Gordon’s goal in the semi final. His shot parried by the keeper to set up Jude Bellingham in the quarter final.

Made a difference every time he came on. His assist justified his inclusion against Argentina.

Rating: 7

‌



Eberechi Eze

Did not get many opportunities but I really liked him against Norway when he changed England’s midfield dynamic.

A good inclusion overall. And you also feel he’d be such a good guy to have around the place.

Rating: 6.5

‌



Bukayo Saka

I regard Saka as one of England’s top three players. He’s so consistent, so reliable and so good.

This was not Bukayo Saka. He was miles off being fit.

He pushed himself at the end of the season to help Arsenal over the line. Arrived unfit - and finished needing a holiday. England in a semi final and not using Saka is unthinkable. That shows how much he has been struggling.

‌



Rating: 6

Should England sack Thomas Tuchel? Have your say in the comments section.

Noni Madueke

‌



Really disappointing tournament. Best from the bench but really arrived with low confidence despite winning the title with Arsenal.

He really needs a summer reset. There’s talent there but he can’t keep getting into positions and wasting crosses.

Rating: 5

Marcus Rashford

‌



Thomas Tuchel made it clear that he likes Rashford but the winger rarely produces on the pitch what he delivers in training.

Another unfulfilled tournament. He’s got so much talent. But we rarely see it for England.

Rating: 5

Anthony Gordon

‌



Frustrating at first and then grew in stature. He also delivered the best interview of the World Cup when he talked about overcoming the odds and proving himself. He did just that.

He scored against Argentina, played well as a forward and covered as a defender. Grew as a player and as a person.

Rating: 7.5

View 7 Images Anthony Gordon scored England's opener against Argentina (Image: Sebastian Widmann - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Ollie Watkins

Six minutes against Panama. Never really got a fair crack - even when Harry Kane looked shattered. Impossible to mark fairly.

Rating: N/A

Ivan Toney

‌



Was it worth it? It didn’t feel like it. I think he deserved more minutes. Instead last gasp against Argentina was too little too late.

Rating: N/A

Harry Kane

England’s Captain Marvel did well overall but was poor against Argentina - when they needed him most.

‌



But after six goals and great leadership, it’s impossible to be critical. Set records, scored and led by example. What a top player and leader.

Rating: 9

Non-playing members: James Trafford, Dean Henderson, Trevoh Chalobah, Kobbie Mainoo

Sports.title: England star 'was not smart' in pivotal Argentina incident that VAR failed to help with
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: England star 'was not smart' in pivotal Argentina incident that VAR failed to help with

England suffered a 2-1 World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina on Wednesday evening, with fans left wondering why VAR didn't intervene in key moments of the match

View Image Djed Spence was seemingly fouled by Lionel Messi (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Djed Spence could have potentially kept England in with a chance at World Cup glory, had he been 'smarter' in the build up to Lautaro Martinez's winning goal for Argentina on Wednesday evening, says Glen Johnson. The Three Lions crumbled almost instantly after taking the lead in the 55th minute of the match at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium through Anthony Gordon.

‌



Rather than looking for a comfortable two-goal cushion, Thomas Tuchel's men were quick to sit in a low block and try to defend a 1-0 lead.

‌



However, with around 40 minutes left to play (including extra-time) that was always going to be too big of a task, considering Argentina's versatility on the front foot.

‌



Chelsea take instant action over Enzo Fernandez post as Argentina crush England hopes READ MORE :

Mark Chapman flies home from World Cup as BBC host misses final round of matches READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez drew his nation level with five minutes left to play, with a silky finish from the edge of the area after being afforded acres of space by John Stones, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers.

Martinez then popped up with the winner two minutes into stoppage time, beating Stones and Ezri Konsa at the back post to header home a 2-1 semi-final win.

However, as Argentinian players wheeled off in celebration, there were claims of foul play from England players directed toward referee Ismail Elfath. Alexis Mac Allister started the move when he was denied by the post from the edge of the area - the ball rolling toward the near side of the pitch.

‌

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
